summary.whatChanges: httpBatchStreamLink now creates an AbortController per operation and merges it with the caller's signal. When a subscriber unsubscribes before the request settles, the link aborts the underlying fetch instead of doing nothing. A test asserts the fetch signal is aborted with an AbortError on unsubscribe.
behaviorChanges: Unsubscribing from an in-flight httpBatchStreamLink query/mutation now aborts the underlying fetch request instead of leaving it running
The operation passed to the batch loader carries a combined signal (caller signal raced with an internal per-operation controller)
No abort is triggered if the request already resolved or rejected (guarded by an isDone flag)
risks: Because operations are batched, aborting one operation's signal may cancel the shared HTTP request and break sibling operations in the same batch, depending on how the batch loader combines signals
Server work is now cancelled on unsubscribe, which changes side-effect behavior for mutations that were previously allowed to complete
`raceAbortSignals` must be imported in this file; the diff does not show the import
The `isDone` flag is set inside promise callbacks, so a synchronous unsubscribe in the same tick as resolution could still fire an abort
